title: π₀.₇: a Steerable Generalist Robotic Foundation Model with Emergent Capabilities
summary: A generalist robot model trained with language, visual subgoals, and task metadata to combine diverse robot and human experience. The authors report improved instruction following and the ability to recombine learned skills in new tasks.
why: Read after π₀ to see how richer conditioning and more varied data change the generalization problem.

title: MEM: Multi-Scale Embodied Memory for Vision Language Action Models
summary: Combines recent video observations with longer-term language memory so robot policies can track task progress and handle missing visual information during extended manipulation tasks.
why: Study how short-term visual detail and long-term task memory solve different problems in a robot policy.

title: RL Token: Bootstrapping Online RL with Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Extracts a compact RL token from a vision-language-action model to train a smaller online reinforcement-learning policy for precise manipulation. The policy adapts without retraining the full VLA.
why: Connect generalist robot pretraining to targeted improvement of difficult contact-rich skills.

title: EgoVerse: An Egocentric Human Dataset for Robot Learning from Around the World
summary: A shared platform and dataset of egocentric human demonstrations for robot learning. The paper studies human-to-robot transfer across labs and robot embodiments, finding that the usefulness of additional human data depends on alignment with robot learning objectives.
why: Read alongside DROID to compare collecting experience with robots against learning from human demonstrations.

title: OA-WAM: Object-Addressable World Action Model for Robust Robot Manipulation
summary: Represents robots and objects with separate persistent slots, predicts how those states evolve, and generates action chunks. The method studies whether explicit object addressing makes manipulation more robust to scene changes.
why: Compare joint world-and-action prediction with reactive VLA policies, focusing on how objects are represented.

title: World-Action Models for Robot Learning and Control: A Survey
summary: Surveys models that connect predictions of future world states to executable robot actions. It organizes their representations, architectures, training pipelines, applications, and evaluation practices.
why: Use this survey to distinguish world models, video predictors, and action-generating WAM systems.

title: Toward Unified Robot Learning: Bridging Representation, Vision-Language-Action, and World Models
summary: Organizes robot learning around representation learning, vision-language-action policies, and world models, then examines how these components interact and where integration remains difficult.
why: A recent overview for connecting perception, action, and prediction before choosing a specialty.

title: From World Models to World Action Models: A Concise Tutorial for Robotics
summary: Introduces the definitions and roles of world models and world action models in robotics, with a framework for comparing their representations, predictions, and interaction mechanisms.
why: Start here for terminology before comparing individual WAM architectures.

title: World Model for Robot Learning: A Comprehensive Survey
summary: Reviews how robot world models support policy learning, planning, learned simulation, and evaluation, connecting these roles to video prediction and embodied applications.
why: Compare what different world models are used for rather than treating all prediction systems as interchangeable.
